svg.aria-label: BCBC 2024 Article 9.20.13.9 Protection of Interior Finish
svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.20.13.9 Protection of Interior Finish
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.20 MASONRY AND INSULATING CONCRETE FORM WALLS NOT IN CONTACT WITH THE GROUND
Protection of Interior Finish

g.text: Interior finish that may be damaged by moisture
Masonry wall: membrane and flashing, (1) and (2)
Wall protected for its full height by the roof of a
carport or porch: Sentence (1) does not apply.

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Except as in Sentence (3), where the interior
finish of the exterior walls may be damaged by
moisture, exterior masonry walls are covered on
the interior surface with sheathing membrane
conforming to CAN/CGSB-51.32-M, lapped not less than
100 mm (3 15/16″) at the joints. This does not apply
to cavity walls, or to walls protected for their
full height by a roof of a carport or porch.
In those situations, flashing is provided where
water will accumulate, to lead it to the
exterior.
Where insulation that effectively limits the
passage of water is applied by a waterproof
adhesive or mortar directly to parged masonry,
the sheathing membrane of Sentence (1) is not
required.
Appendix note
Where a sheathing membrane is not used, the adhesive
or mortar should be applied to form a continuous
bond between the masonry and the insulation.
Drawn: walls cut through, membrane and flashing thickness exaggerated, water path dashed blue. Furring, adhesive and lap positions are illustration only.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.20.13.9. (page 9-151)
